OECDscaleup

Development version. OECDscaleup is under active development, so functions and outputs may still change. Please report problems and suggestions as an issue on GitHub or to scaleup@oecd.org. Use synthetic data in a report (for example from example_scaleup_data()), never confidential firm data.

OECDscaleup computes indicators on high-growth firms (“scalers”) from national firm-level microdata, for the OECD Scale Up project. It is part of the OECD’s work to understand SMEs and their potential to scale up: see Helping SMEs scale up. It builds on previous OECD routines written in Stata.

The firm-level data never leave the national statistical institute that holds them: the package produces aggregate tables, with the statistics needed to check them for confidentiality before they are shared. It covers:

  • the baseline: a firm-year panel of indicators, and tables on the characteristics of scalers, what happens before and after scaling, their contribution to job and turnover creation, and the predictors of scaling;
  • the scaler analysis: the fastest-growing scalers, and scalers that grow into mid-caps;
  • trade (optional): exporters, importers and exporting scalers, from firm-level trade in goods.

Installation

The package is not on CRAN. Install it from GitHub with devtools:

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("amannj/OECDscaleup", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Getting started

  • Get started: a step-by-step walkthrough of the whole analysis on simulated data.
  • Input data and Input data for trade: every input variable, how it is defined and what the package does with it.

In short, with the input files of a country in input_dir:

library(OECDscaleup)

cfg <- config_scaleup(
  country = "FR",
  input_dir = "path/to/input",   # base_financials_FR.dta, ...
  output_dir = "path/to/output",
  nace_revision = "2"            # the NACE revision of the sector codes: "2" or "2.1"
)

check_inputs(cfg)          # checks the input files (counts only)
run_scaleup_pipeline(cfg)  # the baseline tables
run_scaler_analysis(cfg)   # top scalers and scalers to mid-caps
run_trade_pipeline(cfg)    # optional: trade

No real data ship with the package; example_scaleup_data() simulates input data to try it.

Versions

  • The default branch ScalerAnalysis holds the development version described here.
  • The branch Stata-to-R holds version 0.1.0, the first translation of the OECD routines to R.
